file_name: Deliv et al. - 2023 - Development of a video based evidence synthesis knowledge translation resource Drawing on a user cen.txt

barriers.description: Some public participants were known to the lead authors and may have felt pressured not to provide fully critical feedback.
barriers.justification: Social pressure reduced the likelihood of honest critique from participants, hindering facilitation of user involvement and the designers' ability to manage user understanding and evaluate prototypes effectively.
barriers.reference_excerpt: This meant that some of the members of the public involved were known to the lead authors (CD and ET), and therefore may have felt some degree of pressure not to be too critical of the resource for fear of offending.

barriers.description: Participant recruitment relied on a one-week timeframe and convenience/snowball sampling, limiting reach and diversity (e.g., difficulty recruiting minors).
barriers.justification: Short recruitment time and sampling approach constrained the designers' ability to facilitate broad user involvement and to build a comprehensive, representative understanding of context of use.
barriers.reference_excerpt: The timeframe of the recruitment for participants was one week. We used a combination of convenience and snowball sampling via word of mouth ... in the <18 years category where one male was recruited, due to the fact that minors are more difficult to recruit given the necessity of parent/guardian consent.

barriers.description: The project was constrained to an 8-week undergraduate summer student timeline and a €2000 budget, limiting time and funds available.
barriers.justification: Limited time and budget restricted the team's ability to outsource specialist media expertise and to run additional user-testing iterations, impeding prototyping, iterative refinement, and evaluation workloads.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Resource-use for the project was minimal, as this was conducted over 8 weeks as an undergraduate summer student project supported by Evidence Synthesis Ireland for €2000. ... our limited time and resources hindered our ability to outsource expertise (e.g., the hiring of a digital media company ...).

barriers.description: The team collected only minimal participant demographic data (age and gender) and did not gather other personal characteristics.
barriers.justification: Limited participant data reduced designers' ability to develop deep, nuanced, and evolving insights about users, constraining tasks to manage user understanding and to specify detailed user requirements.
barriers.reference_excerpt: People were not offered any incentives for their involvement, and we did not collect any personal characteristics data aside from age and gender.

barriers.description: Researchers (rather than the public) determined the initial key messages due to pragmatic/time constraints, so the approach was not fully user-centred from the outset.
barriers.justification: Starting with researcher-defined messages limited early user involvement and constrained the designers' ability to fully manage user understanding and to specify requirements driven by end-user priorities.
barriers.reference_excerpt: However, our use of researchers to determine the initial key messages of the resource meant that our approach was not fully ‘user-centred’... and given our time restraints, we felt it a necessary pragmatic starting point for those identifying the initial key messages to have a solid understanding of evidence synthesis.
